This is the story of Christine’s family.
On her mother’s side are the Wintrodes, Palatine farmers who
landed at Philadelphia in 1732 and settled in the Pennsylvania
border country near Gettysburg; the Fritzes and Staebells, from Alsace and Bavaria,
who went west to the prairie; and the Jacksons and Duffys of Brooklyn.
On her father’s side are the Maksimows, of Luga in Russia, uprooted by the war,
who spent years in the displaced-persons camps of Germany and reached Paterson,
New Jersey, in 1956. Most of them left little behind: a line in a parish register,
a name in a census, a stone. This film gathers what can still be known of them.
